propositions: CLI write-command argument parsing uses a hand-rolled loop with bespoke semantics (--assignee absent=None sentinel vs explicit empty string) that should be replaced with stdlib argparse while preserving all observable behavior including flag recognition, sentinel values, and error codes

The argparse refactor must preserve command-specific --force semantics (claim: bare --force consumes next non-option token or uses default reason; transition: bare --force sets force_reason to empty string and never consumes following tokens) and the None-vs-empty-string distinction for --assignee and force_reason

The transition._parse_flags function is retained as an argparse-backed shim returning the identical 5-tuple to satisfy three external direct callers in tests that depend on its current return signature and semantics

Unknown/extra tokens must be silently skipped, --help remains dispatcher-served byte-exact from golden help files, abbreviations must not match partial flags, and invalid flags must exit with code 1 not 2
The complexity baseline for _parse_flags must be drained after refactoring drops it below the threshold, and all existing CLI interface and direct-caller tests must pass unchanged
